newsitem.title: USA: NBC, National Geographic to launch cable channel.
newsitem.headline: NBC, National Geographic to launch cable channel.

text.p: National Geographic is going on television worldwide in a joint venture with NBC, the companies said Wednesday.

The glossy monthly magazine with colourful pictures and stories about the world's peoples and places will now fascinate viewers on a new 24-hour channel to be launched by the National Geographic Society and NBC, a unit of General Electric Co., unit in 1997.
Executives declined to detail the cost of the startup and said their business plan has not yet been completed.

The 50-50 joint venture will initially broadcast overseas, most likely in Latin America, Europe and Asia, where the companies are now seeking potential partners. The U.S. launch is likely to come after 1997 as there is no current channel capacity among U.S. cable operators, they said.

"The guts of the relationship will be finding partners in making equity investments in the underlying channel," said Stuart Goldfarb, an NBC senior vice president, in a telephone news conference to launch the channel.
"It's going to be heavily premised on local partners getting involved as equity partners in local (country) channels."
Tim Kelly, president of National Geographic Television, said there were "several hundred hours" of programming available for the new channel.
Kelly said the advertiser-supported channel would include children's and dramatic programming as well as documentaries. Programmes would be broadcast in the local language.
"We expect to produce or acquire a variety of programming for the channel," said Kelly. "A lot of producers are coming to us as filmmakers and broadcast partners."
National Geographic said it expected to continue its broadcasting deals with Turner Broadcasting System Inc. and the Public Broadcasting Service in the United States, which televise its programmes.
National Geographic said it would acquire other programming for the channel.
